questions: Is the graph unweighted (i.e., each edge has length 1) for the purpose of counting operations?
Can pieces move simultaneously in a single operation, or must each operation move exactly one piece?
If the goal state is reached mid-sequence, are further operations counted if they are part of the plan?
Are pieces allowed to pass through each other (i.e., swap positions along an edge) in a single move if it doesn't violate the 'same vertex' rule?
Is the operation count minimized over all possible sequences, including those where pieces might temporarily occupy non-distinct vertices if allowed?
Do we consider the graph to be static, or can edges be traversed multiple times by the same piece?
Is there any constraint on the order of moves, such as alternating between pieces or not?
If the shortest path for A to T and B to S intersect, must we avoid that intersection entirely, or just ensure they are not on the same vertex at the same time?
